picks.title: Apple's camera-equipped AirPods appear in leaked video
picks.excerpt: A promo video surfaced in a macOS beta showing Apple's camera-equipped AirPods, with the assistant narrating "See something you like? Just ask me to save it for later." It is the clearest signal yet that Apple's first always-on visual AI wearable is an audio product, not glasses — a very different interaction model for designers to plan around.
picks.rationale: First moving-picture evidence of Apple's visual-AI wearable, and it shows the interaction model is earless-eyes audio rather than glasses — a concrete brief for anyone designing assistant UX.

picks.title: Google's Pet Memory forgot who my cats are
picks.excerpt: A hands-on review of Gemini for Home's Pet Memory on Nest cameras finds the AI recognition feature confidently mislabeling pets. It is a concrete case study in what happens when an ambient AI feature ships with a confident UI but unreliable perception.
picks.rationale: A shipped Gemini for Home feature whose confident UI outruns its perception — the clearest current example of why ambient AI needs uncertainty designed into the interface.

picks.title: Meta's facial recognition smart glasses idea just resurfaced in a patent
picks.excerpt: A newly public Meta patent describes smart glasses identifying people via AI facial recognition and expression analysis, then using that data to auto-assemble highlight media. It puts the hardest consent-design problem in wearables back on the table.
picks.rationale: Puts face recognition plus expression analysis on the record as a product direction, forcing the consent and disclosure question that every wearable design team is currently deferring.

picks.title: Humanoids flop in first real firefighting drill at World Robot Games
picks.excerpt: At the second World Humanoid Robot Games, 23 teams entered an outdoor firefighting and rescue event and only three survived it. The sharpest available corrective to the humanoid hype cycle, and a useful reality anchor next to the Unitree demo.
picks.rationale: A measured, unstaged test — 23 teams in, 3 finish — that resets expectations for anyone planning products or services around humanoid capability claims.

picks.title: I used AI to create a deli meat-inspired watch face for my Pixel Watch 5 — and now I'm questioning everything
picks.excerpt: A hands-on with the Pixel Watch 5's generative watch-face tool, prompting it into an absurd deli-meat theme. Generative UI on a wearable turns watch faces from a designed asset into a prompt output, with all the taste problems that implies.
picks.rationale: A shipping consumer device where a designed UI asset becomes a prompt output — the first mass-market test of what happens to visual craft when users generate the interface themselves.
